```{r}
#| eval: false

Chaoborus_one_measurement <- ceiling(
  (Biomass_needed_total_mg / Chaoborus_third_instar_DW_mg) *

)
Chaoborus_one_measurement

Chaoborus_total <- Chaoborus_one_measurement * Treatments * Replicates
Chaoborus_total

```

## Feed Chaoborus

::: {.callout-tip title="Protocol 1"}
:::

*Chaoborus* is fed ad libitum with ... Daphnia babies / day. 

*Chaoborus* are fed *Daphnia* neonates ad libitum. *Daphnia* stock is built up in individual jars ahead of assembly, so the stock has to be sized to the neonate demand implied by the *Chaoborus* population above. Sizing that stock starts from two feeding-and-reproduction assumptions, both held with medium confidence: a fourth-instar *Chaoborus* larva eats about 20 neonates (1.25 mm *D. magna*) per feeding (Büns & Ratte, 1991), and an adult *Daphnia* produces about 20 neonates per 5-day clutch cycle. Those small stock jars, each housing a single *Daphnia*, are in turn fed from large (1000 mL) jars, each holding 15 adult *Daphnia* — a high-confidence figure, though the source for it still needs tracking down (see Open questions below).

```{r}
#| label: daphnia-jars
#| eval: false


# Small jars: 1 Daphnia per jar, used to build up the stock.
Jars_small_Daphnia <- ceiling(
  Chaoborus_total / (Daphnia_neonates_born_per_5_days / Daphnia_neonates_per_feeding)
)
Jars_small_Daphnia

Daphnia_per_large_jar <- 15

# Large jars: used to house adults producing the neonate stock.
Jars_big_Daphnia <- ceiling(
  Jars_small_Daphnia / (Daphnia_per_large_jar * Daphnia_neonates_born_per_5_days)
)
Jars_big_Daphnia
```

**Toxicity.** Microcystin-LR concentration will be measured using an ELISA kit. 

*Microcystis aeruginosa* (strain PCC 7806, grown in N-limited modified MLA medium) contains 0.7–7 mg microcystins g⁻¹ DW depending on growth phase (Long et al., 2001). Moving up the food chain, *Daphnia magna* shows roughly 80-fold biodilution relative to *M. aeruginosa* — about 2 mg g⁻¹ DW in the phytoplankton versus ~0.025 mg g⁻¹ DW in *D. magna* (Thostrup & Christoffersen, 1999). Evidence for *Chaoborus* spp. is more mixed: Laurén-Määttä et al. (1995) found no detectable microcystins in *Chaoborus* fed Microcystis-exposed *Daphnia*, though they used HPLC (a comparatively high detection limit) and did not measure toxins in the *Daphnia* themselves; Sotton et al. (2014), a field study using HPLC/PDA, found roughly 5-fold biodilution from zooplankton (863 ng g⁻¹ FW) to *Chaoborus* (168 ng g⁻¹ FW); and Riehle et al. (2024), using high-resolution LC–MS/MS, detected microcystins in zooplankton (2.5–4.5 µg g⁻¹ DW) but not in *Chaoborus*.

Detection limits vary across commercial ELISA kits: the Eurofins Microcystin Plate Kit detects down to 0.05 µg L⁻¹, the Abraxis Microcystins-ADDA ELISA Kit and the Beacon Microcystin ELISA Kit both detect down to 0.10 µg L⁻¹, and the Envirologix Microcystins Quantiplate Kit detects down to 0.15 µg L⁻¹.
